instruction: Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Repair solve(data) for the warehouse cutoff report. cutoff and every at value are integer minutes on the same timeline. Each postings row has a unique string transfer ID, at, state (posted or draft), and units (a positive integer item count). Include each posted transfer dated at or before cutoff. Each receipts row has transfer, at, state (accepted or void), and positive integer units. A receipt belongs to the transfer with that exact ID even if the receipt predates posting. Count every accepted receipt row dated at or before cutoff once, including identical rows representing separate deliveries. Return a list of objects with transfer and remaining (posted units minus counted receipt units). Keep zero and negative balances, omit transfers without an eligible posting, and sort by transfer ID in ascending Python string order. The transfer ID field in both posting and receipt records is named transfer.

Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Implement solve(data) for an audit with integer minute offsets start and end, where start <= end. Each item in samples has an integer minute, an integer temp_c in degrees Celsius, and a state. Only state 'verified' is eligible. At the same minute, the last verified item in input order wins. Return {'opening_c': value} for minute start. Use an exact reading if available. Otherwise interpolate linearly between the closest verified minute before start and the earliest verified minute after start up to and including end. A reading before the audit is eligible regardless of its age. If either interpolation endpoint is missing, return {'opening_c': null}. Do not round.

Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Implement solve(data) for a forecast planner. The input has integer fields weeks (52 or 53 weeks in the fiscal year) and week (1 through weeks, inclusive). Regular forecast checkpoints fall in weeks 1, 5, 9, and every fourth week thereafter through week 49. The final week of the year is also a checkpoint. Return the integer checkpoint week closest to week, measured in whole weeks. An exact midpoint belongs to the later checkpoint. Round within the supplied fiscal year.

Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Implement solve(data) for a short broadcast segment. marker is a nonnegative integer time in milliseconds. cues contains at most 12 objects with a unique lowercase ASCII letter-string id, state, nonnegative integer start and end times in milliseconds with start < end, and an integer score that may be negative. Choose a subset of 'cleared' cues whose half-open intervals [start,end) do not overlap. Touching cues are compatible. At least one selected cue must cover marker. Maximize total score, then minimize cue count, then choose the lexicographically smallest list of IDs in playback order (earliest start first). Return this playback-order list, or [] if no schedule covers the marker.
